display_name: Fritz Haag Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese, Mosel
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr is a steep, slate-dominated site whose sun-trap aspect concentrates ripeness; Fritz Haag harvests for Auslese here to deliver concentrated, high-acid Riesling with clear slate minerality. The name tells you the site; the Auslese designation tells you the grapes were picked at elevated must weight, producing a wine that balances noticeable residual sugar against Mosel’s signature acidity.",
  "wine_summary": "Fritz Haag’s Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr Auslese matters because it pairs a top Mosel vineyard’s Devonian slate soils with late-harvest ripeness; that combination gives a Riesling that reads as sweet-fruited but tensile. The producer works within Mosel’s cool-continent climate—long, slow ripening with strong diurnal shifts—which preserves the high acidity that keeps Auslese wines bright rather than heavy. Critic recognition (TEXSOM silver medals in 2018 and 2020) confirms the bottlings are competitive within the category.",
  "terroir_expression": "The Sonnenuhr terraces sit on weathered Devonian slate (Grauwacke and dark shale) and steep gradients that maximize solar radiation and drainage; slate stores heat and returns it at night, aiding full aromatic ripeness while contributing the flinty, smoky mineral note Mosel Riesling is known for. That geology plus the Mosel valley’s cool, long growing season produces Riesling with lemon-lime and white-peach fruit framed by razor-like acidity and a pronounced mineral streak.",
  "vinification_summary": "As a Prädikat Auslese, this wine is made from selectively harvested, riper grapes—Prädikat classifications denote higher must weights rather than specific vinification techniques—and fermentation typically stops before all sugar is consumed, leaving residual sweetness; low alcohol readings for older vintages (7.0% in 2010, 7.5% in 2011) reflect that balance. Producers in Mosel commonly use gentle pressing and cool-temperature fermentation to preserve aromatics; the result here is pure fruit, restrained yeast influence, and a clear acid/sugar counterpoint.",
  "food_pairing": "1) Spicy Thai green curry with coconut milk — sweetness and high acidity cut through heat and fat while the wine’s lime and stone-fruit notes echo the curry’s aromatics.\n2) Char siu pork buns (bao) — the wine’s residual sugar picks up caramelized pork flavors and acidity refreshes the palate.\n3) Roquefort or a mature blue cheese on walnut toast — the contrast between saline, moldy blue and the wine’s sweet-acid backbone creates satisfying tension.\n4) Seared scallops with brown-butter and lemon — acid sharpens the shellfish while delicate sweetness amplifies the caramelized edges.\n5) Warm apple tart Tatin with crème fraîche — fruit-forward sweetness and citrus lift mirror the wine’s apple/peach notes while acidity keeps the pairing from cloying.",
  "comparable_wines": "J.J. Prüm Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese — why it's comparable: another steep Mosel Sonnenuhr site with slate-driven minerality and bright acidity married to late-harvest fruit. \nSelbach-Oster Zeltinger Sonnenuhr Auslese — why it's comparable: similar steep-slate terroir and a stylistic focus on precision, delivering off-dry to sweet Riesling with pronounced mineral backbone.",
  "style_profile": "Riesling medium-bodied with high acidity and pronounced slate minerality",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink young for primary white-peach and lime fruit, or cellar for 10–30 years to develop petrol, honeyed tertiary notes and softer acid integration. Store at stable 10–12°C on the cork, upright short-term or on side if long-term.",
  "value_assessment": "$40–$90 retail depending on vintage and residual-sugar level; peers at this price include J.J. Prüm and Selbach-Oster Auslese bottlings. The purchase is worth it if you want a terroir-driven Mosel Auslese that trades immediate approachability for long-term development—you get concentrated fruit, slate minerality, and aging potential that more generic late-harvest wines at the same price do not offer.",
  "market_position": "Collectors who focus on Mosel terroir, sommeliers building Riesling-by-vineyard lists, and specialist retailers stock this wine; you’ll find it on German-focused wine lists, wine shops with Old World Riesling programs, and auction lots for mature vintages. parsed.food_pairing:
1) Spicy Thai green curry with coconut milk — sweetness and high acidity cut through heat and fat while the wine’s lime and stone-fruit notes echo the curry’s aromatics.
2) Char siu pork buns (bao) — the wine’s residual sugar picks up caramelized pork flavors and acidity refreshes the palate.
3) Roquefort or a mature blue cheese on walnut toast — the contrast between saline, moldy blue and the wine’s sweet-acid backbone creates satisfying tension.
4) Seared scallops with brown-butter and lemon — acid sharpens the shellfish while delicate sweetness amplifies the caramelized edges.
5) Warm apple tart Tatin with crème fraîche — fruit-forward sweetness and citrus lift mirror the wine’s apple/peach notes while acidity keeps the pairing from cloying.
